as_written_in_papers.quote: Sequencing of the NOD2 gene revealed a novel heterozygous mutation, c.1439 A>G (p.His480Arg) in exon 4, in both patients.
Genetic analysis of NOD2 from the 2 siblings revealed a novel SNV of an H480R mutation in the NACHT region.

cases.statement: Two siblings, both heterozygous: an 8-year-old girl (Case 1, BLAU-ID0091) and her 10-year-old brother (Case 2, BLAU-ID0092). Both had papular rash from 6 months, uveitis and noncaseating granulomas on skin biopsy; Case 1 also had midaortic (thoracoabdominal aortic) stenosis, Case 2 joint involvement.

people.label: Case 1
people.other_allele: not applicable (autosomal dominant); no second NOD2 variant reported
people.key_phenotypes: anterior uveitis; generalized small papules since 6 months; noncaseating granulomatous inflammation on skin biopsy; stenosis of the thoracoabdominal aorta suggestive of midaortic dysplastic syndrome; upper-limb blood pressure higher than lower-limb

quotes.quote: A 8-year-old girl presented with conjunctival injection which was later diagnosed as anterior uveitis that was treated with topical corticosteroid.
She reported having generalized multiple small papules (Fig. 1A) since the age of 6 months.
A skin biopsy of her lower limbs showed noncaseating granulomatous inflammation (Fig. 1B).

Echocardiogram and computed tomography (CT) angiogram revealed stenosis of the thoracoabdominal aorta with diffuse luminal narrowing from the aortic isthmus to the suprarenal arteries (Fig. 2), suggestive of midaortic dysplastic syndrome.
On presentation, her blood pressure as measured in the upper extremities was 126/60 mmHg.

people.label: Case 2
people.other_allele: not applicable (autosomal dominant); no second NOD2 variant reported
people.key_phenotypes: small erythematous papules from 6 months; subcutaneous nodules at wrists and ankles; pain in multiple lower-limb joints (arthritic changes); uveitis from early childhood with corneal subepithelial opacities and posterior synechia; noncaseating granulomatous inflammation on skin biopsy

quotes.quote: He had small erythematous papules of 1–2 mm in size in both arms (Fig. 3A).
He had subcutaneous nodules in the wrists and ankles.
He complained of pain in multiple lower limb joints, especially while sitting down or squatting, indicating arthritic changes.
His eye exam revealed multiple mild subepithelial opacities on both eyes (Fig. 4) along with focal posterior synechia.
A skin biopsy of his lower limbs showed noncaseating granulomatous inflammation (Fig. 3B).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Both siblings had granulomatous skin disease confirmed by biopsy, uveitis and (Case 2) joint involvement, which the authors relate to the Blau triad. The authors note that Case 1's vascular involvement is not a common Blau feature. Routine blood tests were normal; no other genes or panels were tested.

quotes.quote: In our case report, both siblings exhibited skin rash from 6months of age, which is consistent with BS.
Case 1 in our report exhibited vascular involvements, which is not a very common feature of BS.
Laboratory tests including complete blood cell count (CBC), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and thyroid function tests were all normal.
Under the suspicion of familial granulomatous disease, genetic analysis for BS was performed.

segregation.statement: Two affected siblings both carry the variant. Three further affected paternal relatives (father with uveitis and minimal rash; paternal aunt and her daughter diagnosed with sarcoidosis) were not genotyped because DNA was unavailable. Paternal grandparents reportedly had no significant symptoms and were not genotyped. No unaffected relative was tested.

quotes.quote: Sequencing of the NOD2 gene revealed a novel heterozygous mutation, c.1439 A>G (p.His480Arg) in exon 4, in both patients.
Their father (38 years) was also affected by uveitis but with minimal skin rashes.
The paternal aunt (39 years) and her daughter (13 years) were diagnosed as sarcoidosis.
Unfortunately, DNA samples of other family members were unavailable.
The father, paternal aunt and her daughter showing sarcoidosis like features are very likely to have mutation consistent with BS, although we were not able to confirm this with genetic analysis.

As BS is inherited in autosomal dominant fashion, one can expect that one of the paternal grandparents to have been effected by BS but neither of the paternal grandparents showed significant symptoms.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo by the authors' account (familial, presumed paternal inheritance); no parent was genotyped.

quotes.quote: The family pedigree in our case strongly indicates that the BS mutation is inherited through the paternal side of the family.

functional.statement: No functional assay of this variant; the authors say it would be of interest to test NF-kB activation.

quotes.quote: It would be of interest to see if the novel mutation in H480R also leads to NF-κB activation.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense (predicted p.His453Arg on NP_001357395.1), stated by the authors to lie in the NACHT region. The authors describe NACHT-domain mutations in general as gain-of-function (gene-level statement, not shown for this variant).

quotes.quote: Genetic analysis of NOD2 from the 2 siblings revealed a novel SNV of an H480R mutation in the NACHT region.

Because the activation of NOD2 involves oligomerization initiated by the NACHT-domain, mutations in this domain may decrease the threshold for spontaneous oligomerization of NOD210), and this gain-of-function mutation leads to the hyper-activation of NF-κB2).

population_data_in_papers.statement: Absent from an in-house exome database of 250 Korean individuals.

quotes.quote: This single nucleotide variant (SNV) was not found in the in-house database containing the exomes of 250 Korean individuals7).

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a novel NOD2 mutation that causes Blau syndrome; no ACMG criteria are given.

quotes.quote: We report a novel NOD2 genetic mutation that causes BS.
In conclusion, our report identifies a novel mutation in NOD2 gene that lead to a familiar case of BS.

concerns: Legacy numbering: the paper writes c.1439 A>G (p.His480Arg) with no transcript; the batch places it as NM_001370466.1:c.1358A>G, predicted p.(His453Arg). The 81-nt and 27-residue offsets match the older NM_022162 numbering (protein_check: differs, stated H480R, predicted H453R). The panel should confirm the placement.

The two carriers (BLAU-ID0091 and BLAU-ID0092) are siblings in one family, so they are two people but not independent observations; segregation rests on two affected siblings only, as the three affected paternal relatives were not genotyped.
Case 1's midaortic dysplastic syndrome is an atypical feature that the authors themselves flag; the paper does not report testing for other causes of aortic stenosis.
The father, aunt and cousin are inferred carriers only ('very likely to have mutation'); the aunt and cousin carry a sarcoidosis diagnosis, not a genetic Blau diagnosis.
The extent of NOD2 sequencing (all exons or exon 4 only) is not stated.
notes_for_panel: Familial case: two genotyped affected siblings with biopsy-proven granulomatous dermatitis and uveitis, three further affected but untested paternal relatives. Absent from 250 in-house Korean exomes; no functional or in-silico data. Paper uses legacy numbering (c.1439A>G / H480R), translated by the batch to MANE c.1358A>G / H453R.
